brands.description: The Print Shop is a basic desktop publishing software package developed in the early 1980s by Brøderbund. It was unique in that it provided libraries of clip-art and templates through a simple interface to build signs, posters and banners with household dot-matrix printers. Over the years the software has been updated to accommodate changing file formats and printer technologies.

transcript.text: Welcome to On Print Shop.
In this tutorial, we'll walk you through how to manage product filters, from enabling an option as a filter to configuring personalized filters and understanding how they appear on the storefront.
From the Add or Edit Product option screen, you'll now see a toggle named Use in Product Filter under the Presentation Settings section.
When you enable this setting, the selected option will appear as a filter on the storefront.
This works only for option types like Radio, drop down and checkbox.
Now to create a personalized filter, go to the newly introduced Product Filter section in the Product option screen.
The process has two main steps, creating the filter by adding the title and type and then adding the filter options.
To start creating filters, click on the Add button and then give your filter a name that customers will see on the storefront, such as Material.
Choose how the filter options will appear, such as text labels like nylon or linen, images like glossy or matte, or color swatches like red, blue, or black.
You can also turn the filter on or off and set its sort order to decide where it appears.
Once you have created the filter, it's time to add options to it.
Click on the Save and Continue, or else click on the Save and then click on the Add button from the respective Edit Product Filter screen.
Now choose the type of filter product specific to link the filter to certain products not available if you choose image or color, display types or attribute specific to base it on product features.
Attribute specific filters can be created by combining multiple attributes into one filter option, or by selecting a single product option and choosing which of its attributes to include.
When using the single attribute method, you'll see a table listing all features of the selected option.
You can tick the ones you want, rename them, add an image or colour if allowed, set their order and enable or disable them.
Only selected and active options will appear on the storefront, and some fields like title, upload, image and select colour won't be shown in this method.
On the Product Filters list screen, you can view all the filters you've created.
A search box is available to help you quickly find specific filters.
Each filter is displayed with key details including its serial number, title, display type, status, sort order, and actions such as Edit to modify the filter or Delete to remove it.

On the storefront, any filters created either from the product filter screen or marked as Use in Product Filter from the Edit or Add Product option screen will be displayed on relevant product category pages, except for B2B stores where filters are not shown.
These filters appear below the category section in a collapsible panel, allowing users to search within options.
Selected filters are shown in a pill format below the product list with options to remove individual filters or clear all at once.
If no product under a category has the related option, the filter won't appear.
Additionally, when filters are available, they replace the default left side bow on that category page.
That's all for this tutorial on adding and managing product filters.
With this, you can create, customize, and organize filters to help customers find exactly what they're looking for, making their shopping experience faster and more enjoyable.
Thank you for watching.
We hope this new product filter makes it easier for your customers to find the right products quickly and enhances their shopping experience.
If you have any questions, our support executives are here to help.
Just reach out through live chat on on printshop.com.
Thanks for tuning in.
